A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LightTransfer work. Their main text, figures, tables, equations, and appendices A–G are available and can be matched despite the publication-format change.

before.justification: v2 reports original LongBench, NIAH, mathematical-reasoning, throughput, and ablation results in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains those experiments and adds head-wise comparisons, MoE results, deployment measurements, and output-distribution analysis.

M1.justification: Lazy-ratio scoring, priority-queue pruning, streaming attention, and frequency-based layer selection followed by fine-tuning are retained. Section 5.1 corrects 'largest' to 'lowest' for the ratios of layers retaining full attention; both versions already specify removing the highest-ratio layers, so this resolves a wording inconsistency rather than changing the procedure.

E1.justification: The benchmark families remain unchanged. v3 explicitly reports 2WikiMultihopQA and MultiFieldQA-ZH in its new LongBench analyses, but v2 says it prints only 16 of 21 tasks for space reasons. The PDFs do not establish whether these tasks were previously unevaluated or merely unreported. The added MoE and Gradient backbones are model-setting changes.

E2.justification: Section 6.2 adds mathematical-reasoning comparisons with MiniCache-Test, SqueezeAttention-Test, and DuoAttention. Appendix C.3 adds RazorAttention, HeadKV, and DuoAttention comparisons, and C.5 adds Shapley-based and BERTology layer-selection baselines. These substantially expand the evaluated comparison set; FastGen is discussed without a reported comparison row.

E3.justification: New protocols include 50%-sparsity head-wise comparisons using the Gradient checkpoint and full LongBench inputs to calibrate RazorAttention/HeadKV (C.3), controlled TP versus DP+TP testing on eight A100-40GB GPUs from 4K to 512K tokens (B.2), and prefilling KL comparisons with zero versus 50% layer reduction (B.3). Original benchmark settings remain unchanged; BF16 is newly disclosed rather than a demonstrated precision change.

E4.justification: v3 adds a deployment throughput/memory analysis comparing parallelization strategies (B.2), a distribution-discrepancy analysis intended to assess the error bound (B.3), and additional layer-selection comparisons at a common inference budget (C.5). Existing retention-ratio, hyperparameter, SnapKV-combination, and attention-pattern analyses remain.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run or seed counts, confidence intervals, standard deviations, or significance tests. The added tables continue to report point estimates.

E6.justification: Original LongBench, mathematical-reasoning, throughput, and hyperparameter scores are retained. New Table 4 reports LightTransfer-Test scores of 85.0 on MathOAI and 40.0 on AIME24; Tables 6 and 8–11 add deployment, KL, head-wise, MoE, and strategy results. Table 9 reports averages of 40.64 for LightTransfer and 40.98 for DuoAttention under the new Gradient-checkpoint comparison, not a same-setting improvement over v2.

T1.justification: Theorem 5.1, Assumptions F.1–F.2, Theorem F.3, and the supporting lemmas and proofs retain their mathematical substance. Appendix B.3 adds an empirical analysis and interpretation, not a revised bound, definition, or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: lightweight conversion through lazy-layer identification, training-free long-context adaptation or minimal reasoning fine-tuning, up to 2.17× throughput, less than 1.5% LongBench loss, and 53.3% AIME24 accuracy.

C2.justification: v3 expands deployment explanations involving parameter replication, memory limits, and load balancing (B.2), and adds limitations concerning test-versus-training performance and fine-tuning versus native hybrid training (B.4). It also newly claims that near-zero KL values establish bound tightness (B.3), although the negative reported estimates and absence of a numerical bound comparison do not substantiate that interpretation.

D1.justification: Appendix A newly specifies PyTorch/HuggingFace, flash_attention_with_kvcache, BF16 weights/activations/KV caches, and absence of quantization. The new deployment study specifies SGLang and an eight-A100-40GB node. These improve documentation without establishing implementation changes to retained experiments; project-access information is unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 adds references supporting head-wise pruning, alternative layer-importance strategies, and Qwen-MoE, and emphasizes its calibration-free positioning against DuoAttention and related methods. The main related-work narrative and positioning around lightweight transformer-to-hybrid conversion remain largely unchanged.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and the main section order are retained. Changes include the largest/lowest correction, clarification of the QwQ-STILL distillation setup, expanded figure explanation, and additional appendix subsections; the existing narrative is not extensively rewritten.

P2.justification: The main text changes from two columns to a single-column journal layout, with widespread figure/table resizing and relocation. Table 2 replaces colored model-group backgrounds with gray LightTransfer-row highlighting, and six new tables are added. Existing result plots are retained; Figure 2 is redrawn and its caption expands the explanation of attention aggregation.

improvement.justification: Additional head-wise and layer-selection comparisons, deployment measurements, implementation disclosures, and explicit limitations improve empirical scrutiny and make the paper easier to assess. Reporting problems limit these gains: Table 8's negative KL estimates do not establish tightness of the unchanged bound, and Table 11 overstates the HotpotQA margin over the next-best baseline—43.70 versus 42.48 is 1.22 points, not 3.7. The original method and main results remain intact.
